blindReviewDeclaration: I formed the bounded independent DESIGN verdict before reading any author intake. The pre-verdict source-first review was limited to the round-2 checklist's closed source list and revalidated only the manifest self-surface correction, checker-required standalone authority colon/hash binding, and the current-invocation rootRunId receipt design. I read the author material only after that verdict for comparison; it did not alter this verdict.
expectedBehavior: THCL-U01 declares the existing remediation manifest path as update, so the existing implementation-design-granularity checker no longer treats its self-referential hash binding as a create of an already-existing path.

The detailed design and separately hash-bound design-only authorization each contain the checker-required standalone implementationAuthority: false colon form, and the remediation manifest binds their current SHA-256 bytes.

VERIFY_ROOT generates one rootRunId before any child execution, derives the receipt path from that invocation identity, and supplies that same identity with the receipt path to U12 through --expected-root-run-id.

U12 remains a pure receipt validator: it compares the supplied current rootRunId and derived receipt-path identity exactly, rejects a structurally valid prior receipt, and never spawns a second child execution.
VERIFY_ROOT remains the sole VERIFY_CHILD executor; the ACTIVE GATE child exact set and ARCHUNIT_SELECTOR receipt remain separate.

This is static DESIGN review only; it makes no implementation, test, runner, contract, dynamic execution, business, cleanup, performance, Testcontainers, DEV, L2, seed, reset, browser, UAT, or deployment claim.

solutionReasonableness.problemFit: Changing only the manifest self-path disposition from create to update directly removes the checker-admission contradiction without weakening the checker. The existing colon-form authority declarations and their manifest hashes remain mechanically bound. The root-generated identity, derived receipt path, and caller-supplied expected rootRunId give the pure validator the minimum information required to reject a replayed prior receipt.
solutionReasonableness.simplerAlternativeAssessment: Relaxing the create-path rule, treating prose authority as sufficient, accepting receipt self-attestation, using a timestamp heuristic, or allowing U12 to execute children would either weaken a current control or duplicate execution. The accepted correction and same-invocation identity transport are the smaller bounded design.
solutionReasonableness.costFit: The correction is limited to the manifest's self-referential disposition. Revalidation preserves the existing checker, catalog, root executor, and validator roles; it introduces no new gate, execution map, runtime action, or implementation authority.

conclusion.summary: Static DESIGN review GO. THCL-U01's remediation manifest now correctly declares its own existing hash-binding surface as update, so the existing checker can admit the two-unit design. Both authority artifacts retain checker-required standalone colon form and current manifest hash bindings. THCL-U02's design keeps rootRunId generated once by VERIFY_ROOT, derives the receipt path from that current invocation, passes expected identity to a pure U12 validator, rejects a valid prior receipt, and preserves selector separation and single child execution. No M or S findings. Static DESIGN only.
